title: Ahrefs vs Moz: Compare SEO Research Workflows
description: Compare Ahrefs and Moz for backlink research, keyword discovery, site audits and rank tracking. Use a repeatable test and verify current plan limits directly with each vendor.

features.name: Primary use
features.tool1Detail: Evaluate backlink research, competitor-page discovery, keyword research, site auditing and rank tracking against the tasks your team performs.
features.tool2Detail: Evaluate keyword research, link analysis, site crawling and rank tracking against the same task list.

features.name: Backlink research
features.tool1Detail: Use a fixed set of client or test domains. Record relevant referring domains discovered, export usefulness and the manual checks needed to validate findings.
features.tool2Detail: Run the same domains and questions. Compare coverage and useful findings, and validate important links rather than treating any third-party index as complete.

features.name: Keyword and competitor research
features.tool1Detail: Test a consistent keyword set and competing pages. Check whether suggestions are relevant to the search intent, geography and client niche.
features.tool2Detail: Use the same seeds, locations and competitor pages. Record useful ideas, missing data and the effort needed to turn findings into recommendations.

features.name: Technical site audits
features.tool1Detail: Crawl a representative set of pages and compare reported problems with issues you have independently confirmed. Record false positives and missed issues.
features.tool2Detail: Use the same crawl scope and known test cases. Check crawl access, prioritization, explanations and whether findings can be converted into practical tickets.

features.name: Rank tracking and reporting
features.tool1Detail: Before purchase, verify supported locations, update cadence, keyword limits, history and exports for the exact plan.
features.tool2Detail: Verify the same requirements directly with the vendor. Do not assume report branding, scheduled delivery or a particular export is included.

features.name: Pricing and limits
features.tool1Detail: Plan prices, usage limits and entitlements can change. Compare a dated official quote or pricing page, billing interval, project limits, seats and any overages.
features.tool2Detail: Use the same currency, billing period, team size and workflow assumptions. Keep unknowns visible and request clarification from the vendor instead of estimating.

verdict: Ahrefs and Moz overlap in several SEO research workflows, but a universal winner cannot be substantiated here without a current, reproducible test and verified plan-level evidence. Start with the tasks that drive your service: backlink and competitor-page research, keyword discovery, technical audits, or rank tracking. Run the same sample domains and questions in both products, manually validate important findings, and compare the time required to produce a useful client recommendation. Then confirm current prices, project and keyword limits, seats, exports, and reporting entitlements directly with each vendor. Choose the product that performs your required work reliably at a sustainable total cost—not the one with the highest unsupported score.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Ahrefs and Moz?
faqs.answer: Both support SEO research, but the most useful distinction depends on your workflow and the results you can validate. Compare them using the same domains, keyword questions, competitor pages and technical audit cases instead of relying on a generic feature list.

faqs.question: Which tool is better for an SEO agency?
faqs.answer: There is no verified universal winner in this comparison. Agencies should test client-project capacity, backlink and keyword research, technical audit quality, rank tracking, exports, reporting and team access on the exact plans they would buy.

faqs.question: How should I compare their prices?
faqs.answer: Check each vendor's current official pricing and plan documentation. Normalize currency, billing interval, number of users, projects, tracked keywords, crawl usage, exports, required add-ons and contract terms. Save the date checked because packaging can change.

faqs.question: Can I rely on backlink or keyword metrics as exact numbers?
faqs.answer: Treat third-party SEO metrics as estimates. Verify consequential findings against first-party analytics and Search Console where available, live pages, crawl evidence and the actual business context.

faqs.question: What is the fairest way to test both products?
faqs.answer: Choose a small representative set of domains and a fixed task list, run the same tasks in both products, validate a sample of findings, time the work, record gaps and manual effort, and compare total cost only after confirming current plan limits.

faqs.question: How should I interpret the winner on this page?
faqs.answer: Treat any stored winner label as a provisional editorial starting point unless this page explicitly marks it as verified. A winner label is not proof of a controlled hands-on benchmark or a universally best product. Match the choice to your requirements, verify current vendor documentation and plan limits, and run the same representative tasks in both products before deciding.

faqs.question: Were both products independently tested for this comparison?
faqs.answer: This comparison does not claim a verified, controlled hands-on benchmark unless a dated test method and results are explicitly provided. Use the feature-by-feature checklist as a decision aid, confirm plan-specific capabilities with official vendor documentation, and record your own pilot results before relying on a purchase decision.

faqs.question: How do I compare the real total cost?
faqs.answer: Compare the current vendor quote for the same number of paid seats, billing term, region and currency. Include required feature tiers, guest or viewer access, automation or usage limits, storage, integrations, exports, support, taxes, renewal terms, migration work and ongoing administration. Recheck official pricing and contract terms before purchase because packaging can change.
